---
title: "Visualising the collected cell death area scores"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
---

Date: 8/5/26

In this document I conduct exploratory data analysis of the cell death area score dataset by visualising scoring patterns with ggplot2 in R.

---

## 1. Setup

### 1.1 Load required packages

```{r}
# 1.1
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(here)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(patchwork)
library(png)
library(tiff)
```

### 1.2 Load data

Data loaded from the output of `01_generate_raw_data/04_median_and_centre_coords`. Scorer IDs are already anonymised (1–10).

```{r}
# 1.2
path_data <- here("analyses", "01_generate_raw_data", "04_median_and_centre_coords", "combined_cda_data_median.csv")

raw_data <- read_csv(path_data, show_col_types = FALSE)

score_data <- raw_data %>%
  select(Basename, Row, Col, Pos, Scorer1, Score1, Scorer2, Score2, Scorer3, Score3, Median_Score) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(Scorer1, Scorer2, Scorer3), as.character),
    across(c(Score1, Score2, Score3), as.character)
  )

score_data_no0 <- score_data %>%
  filter(Median_Score != 0)

head(score_data)

print(nrow(score_data))
```

There are 6,364 rows.

### 1.3 Helper functions and colour palettes

```{r}
# 1.3.1
gen_long <- function(data) {
  long <- data %>%
    select(
      Basename, Row, Col, Pos, Median_Score,
      Scorer1, Score1, Scorer2, Score2, Scorer3, Score3
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols          = c(Scorer1, Score1, Scorer2, Score2, Scorer3, Score3),
      names_to      = c(".value", "num"),
      names_pattern = "(Scorer|Score)(\\d+)"
    ) %>%
    select(-num) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Scorer))

  long$Scorer <- factor(long$Scorer, levels = sort(as.numeric(unique(long$Scorer))))
  long
}

save_plot <- function(p, filename, width, height, dir = "supp_plots") {
  ggsave(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", dir, filename),
    plot = p, width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 300
  )
}

# Severity palette: pale yellow (0 = no cell death) → deep red (6 = strong cell death).
# Sequential YlOrRd is colourblind-safe (the previous RdYlGn red-green scale was not).
sev_pal <- setNames(brewer.pal(7, "YlOrRd"), as.character(0:6))

# Direction palette for signed distance plots
dir_pal <- c("Above" = "firebrick", "At" = "grey60", "Below" = "#3182bd")
```

```{r}
# 1.3.2
score_data_long <- gen_long(score_data)

score_data_valid <- score_data_long %>%
  filter(!grepl("\\[\\]", Score), !is.na(Score)) %>%
  mutate(Score = as.integer(Score))
```

---

## 2. Raw scores

### 2.1 Example CDAs and scoring key

```{r}
# 2.1
# Scoring key (scores 0-6, left to right). The original key is a CMYK JPEG, so an
# sRGB copy (converted via its ICC profile) is read here to keep colours faithful.
# The number strip is cropped off (rows 189-554 keep just the 7 panels). The example
# columns carry the score labels and are boxed to the same width as the key panels.
key <- readPNG(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", "assets", "lesion_score_key_rgb.png"))
key_raster <- as.raster(key[189:554, , 1:3])
W <- dim(key)[2] # key width (px)
key_h <- length(189:554) # cropped key height (panels only)

# key panel edges (measured) -> example column boxes match these exactly
L <- c(7, 404, 801, 1195, 1586, 1978, 2369)
R <- c(389, 786, 1180, 1571, 1963, 2354, 2745)
cen <- (L + R) / 2

# Four random example CDAs per score (0-6)
set.seed(42)
n_per <- 4
thumbs <- lapply(0:6, function(sc) {
  files <- list.files(here("data", "cropped_images", sc), full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.tif$")
  lapply(sample(files, n_per), function(f) as.raster(readTIFF(f)))
})

# Layout in pixel units (bottom to top): key panels, "Scoring Key" title, grid of boxed examples, score labels.
# Boxes are centred on the key panels but a little narrower, leaving clear gaps between columns.
box_hw <- 160
pad <- 16
tgap <- 12
side <- 2 * box_hw - 2 * pad
title_band <- 150
lab_band <- 150
box_h <- n_per * side + (n_per - 1) * tgap + 2 * pad
g0 <- key_h + title_band # grid (box) bottom
g1 <- g0 + box_h # grid (box) top
Htot <- g1 + lab_band

boxes <- data.frame(xmin = cen - box_hw, xmax = cen + box_hw, ymin = g0, ymax = g1)

thumb_layers <- list()
for (j in 1:7) {
  for (i in seq_len(n_per)) {
    ytop <- g1 - pad - (i - 1) * (side + tgap)
    thumb_layers <- c(
      thumb_layers,
      annotation_raster(thumbs[[j]][[i]],
        xmin = cen[j] - side / 2, xmax = cen[j] + side / 2,
        ymin = ytop - side, ymax = ytop, interpolate = TRUE
      )
    )
  }
}

p <- ggplot() +
  annotation_raster(key_raster, xmin = 0, xmax = W, ymin = 0, ymax = key_h, interpolate = TRUE) +
  annotate("text", x = W / 2, y = key_h + title_band / 2, label = "Scoring Key", size = 7) +
  thumb_layers +
  geom_rect(
    data = boxes, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = cen, y = g1 + lab_band / 2, label = 0:6, size = 8) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, W), ylim = c(0, Htot), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void()

ggsave(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", "thesis_plots", "cdaexamples.png"),
  p,
  width = W / 300, height = Htot / 300, dpi = 300, device = ragg::agg_png, bg = "white"
)
knitr::include_graphics(here("analyses", "02_score_distributions", "thesis_plots", "cdaexamples.png"))
```

**What this shows:**

- Four randomly selected example CDAs for each median score (0-6, upper panel), aligned above the published scoring key (lower panel).
- Within a score class there is substantial variation (lighting, veins, damage, black background regions), while distant classes are clearly distinguishable and adjacent classes can be hard to tell apart.

### 2.2 Score counts (all scores and median scores)

```{r fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
# 2.2
all_counts <- score_data_valid %>%
  count(Score, name = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Score = factor(Score, levels = 0:6))

median_counts <- score_data %>%
  count(Median_Score, name = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Median_Score = factor(as.integer(Median_Score), levels = 0:6))

# Largest-remainder rounding so displayed percentages sum to exactly 100.0
pct_sum_100 <- function(counts, digits = 1) {
  scaled <- counts / sum(counts) * 100 * 10^digits
  floor_vals <- floor(scaled)
  deficit <- round(100 * 10^digits) - sum(floor_vals)
  top_up <- order(-(scaled - floor_vals))[seq_len(deficit)]
  floor_vals[top_up] <- floor_vals[top_up] + 1
  floor_vals / 10^digits
}

all_counts <- all_counts %>% mutate(Pct = pct_sum_100(Count))
median_counts <- median_counts %>% mutate(Pct = pct_sum_100(Count))

cat("All-score counts:\n")
print(all_counts)
cat(sprintf("(percentages sum to %.1f)\n", sum(all_counts$Pct)))
cat("\nMedian score counts:\n")
print(median_counts)
cat(sprintf("(percentages sum to %.1f)\n", sum(median_counts$Pct)))

most_common_median <- median_counts[which.max(median_counts$Count), ]
least_common_median <- median_counts[which.min(median_counts$Count), ]
cat(sprintf(
  "\nMost common median score class:  %s (n = %d, %.1f%%)\n",
  most_common_median$Median_Score, most_common_median$Count, most_common_median$Pct
))
cat(sprintf(
  "Least common median score class: %s (n = %d, %.1f%%)\n",
  least_common_median$Median_Score, least_common_median$Count, least_common_median$Pct
))

p_all <- ggplot(all_counts, aes(x = Score, y = Count, fill = Score)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Score", y = "Frequency (All Scorers)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

p_median <- ggplot(median_counts, aes(x = Median_Score, y = Count, fill = Median_Score)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Score", y = "Frequency (Median Only)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

p <- p_all + p_median
p
save_plot(p, "score_counts.png", width = 12, height = 6, dir = "thesis_plots")
```

**What this shows:**

- The left panel shows each individual score collected across all scorers. The right panel counts the median score of each CDA, which will be used as the ground-truth label.
- 0 is by far the most common score in both views.
- Intermediate scores (3-4) are more numerous than higher (5-6) or lower (1-2)

### 2.3 Dotplot of all scores, sorted by median score

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8
# 2.3
score_data_raw <- score_data %>%
  mutate(across(c(Score1, Score2, Score3), ~ replace(., . == "[]", NA_character_)))

score_data_sorted <- score_data_raw %>%
  arrange(Median_Score) %>%
  mutate(row_index = row_number())

boundary_df <- score_data_sorted %>%
  group_by(Median_Score) %>%
  summarize(boundary = max(row_index)) %>%
  mutate(boundary = boundary - 0.5)

group_labels <- score_data_sorted %>%
  group_by(Median_Score) %>%
  summarize(center = mean(row_index), .groups = "drop")

p <- ggplot(score_data_sorted, aes(x = row_index, y = Score)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score1)), alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score2)), alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score3)), alpha = 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(data = boundary_df, aes(xintercept = boundary), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(
    data = group_labels,
    aes(x = center, y = 6.45, label = as.integer(Median_Score)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fontface = "bold", size = 5
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 0, y = 6.45, label = "Median score:",
    hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 5
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6, limits = c(0, 6.6)) +
  labs(x = "CDA Index", y = "Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p
save_plot(p, "dotplot_scores_sorted_by_median.png", 14, 8)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows the spread of scores collected for each cell death area. The X axis is grouped by median score.
- Scorers often provide disagreeing scores for the same image, and these disagreeing scores are most commonly adjacent to the median score, although a smaller number may be much further away.
- The median score 0 group appears to have fewer disagreeing scores.

### 2.4 Dotplot of all scores, faceted by median score

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=14}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14
# 2.4
set.seed(123)
score_data_random <- score_data_raw[sample(nrow(score_data_raw)), ]
score_data_random$row_index <- seq_len(nrow(score_data_random))

desired_order <- c("6", "5", "4", "3", "2", "1", "0")
score_data_random$Median_Score <- factor(as.integer(score_data_random$Median_Score), levels = desired_order)

p <- ggplot(score_data_random, aes(x = row_index, y = as.numeric(Score))) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score1)), color = "black", alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score2)), color = "black", alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(y = as.numeric(Score3)), color = "black", alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 6)) +
  labs(x = "CDA Index", y = "Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~Median_Score, ncol = 2) +
  theme(
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title   = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p
save_plot(p, "all_scores.png", 10, 14)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows the spread of scores collected for each median score group in a slightly different format, allowing patterns of disagreement to be more clearly visualised for smaller, non-0 classes.

## 3. Score frequencies by scorer

### 3.1 Score frequency by scorer (bubble)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
# 3.1
score_freq <- score_data_valid %>%
  group_by(Scorer, Score) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

p <- ggplot(score_freq, aes(x = Scorer, y = Score)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = factor(Score)), stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = 4, color = "black", size = 5) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Frequency", range = c(0.06, 25)) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Score", values = sev_pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(x = "Scorer", y = "Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.6, 6.2))
p
save_plot(p, "score_freq.png", width = 10, height = 12)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows how many of each score was collected by each scorer.
- For all scorers, 0 was the most commonly collected score.
- Different scorers collected a different number of scores. Scorer 5 in particular seems to have collected fewer scores than other scorers.

### 3.2 Score percentage by scorer (heatmap)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
# 3.2
score_pct <- score_freq %>%
  group_by(Scorer) %>%
  mutate(proportion = Count / sum(Count))

scorer_totals <- score_freq %>%
  group_by(Scorer) %>%
  summarise(Total = sum(Count), .groups = "drop")

scorer_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(scorer_totals$Scorer, "\n(n=", scorer_totals$Total, ")"),
  as.character(scorer_totals$Scorer)
)

p <- ggplot(score_pct, aes(x = Scorer, y = factor(Score), fill = proportion)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", proportion * 100)), color = "black", size = 4.5, vjust = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(name = "Proportion", low = "white", high = "firebrick") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scorer_labels) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Scorer", y = "Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
p
save_plot(p, "score_pct.png", width = 10, height = 7)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows distribution of scores collected by each scorer as a percentage. It removes the replaces the count variable, making comparisons between scorers easier.
- It shows that the number of 0s collected by scorer 5 is indeed lower than any other scorer, and the number of 6s higher than any other scorer.
- It shows patterns that could be attributed to certain scoring behaviours. For example, scorer 10 collected many more 1s than any other scorer, but very few 0s. Scorer 10 may have a different approach to differentiating between these scores than other scorers. In contrast, scorer 1 collected almost no 1s or 2s, but many 0s.
- Some scorers (1, 5, 7) scored far fewer cell death areas than others.

## 4. Missing scores

### 4.1 Missing score frequency by scorer and median score (bubble)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
# 4.1
score_data_nas <- score_data_long %>%
  filter(Score == "[]" | is.na(Score))

if (nrow(score_data_nas) > 0) {
  nas_freq <- score_data_nas %>%
    group_by(Scorer, Median_Score) %>%
    summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

  p <- ggplot(nas_freq, aes(x = Scorer, y = Median_Score)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = factor(Median_Score)), stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = 4, color = "black", size = 5) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Frequency", range = c(1.19, 25)) +
    scale_color_manual(name = "Median\nScore", values = sev_pal) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
    labs(x = "Scorer", y = "Median Score") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.6, 6.2))
  print(p)
  save_plot(p, "missing_scores.png", width = 10, height = 12)
} else {
  message("No missing scores in canonical data.")
}
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows the number of scores that were missed by each scorer. A missed score means that a scorer did not record an annotation for a cell death area which was scored by two other scorers. The median score on this plot is the agreed score of the remaining two scorers who did record an annotation.
- The majority of missed scores were on class 0 cell death areas.
- Scorer 10 missed far more scores than others - 36 compared to the next nearest of 23.

## 5. Distance from median

### 5.1 Signed distance from median by scorer (bubble)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=14}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14
# 5.1
dist_data <- score_data_valid %>%
  mutate(
    Distance_to_Median = Score - Median_Score,
    Direction = case_when(
      Distance_to_Median > 0 ~ "Above",
      Distance_to_Median < 0 ~ "Below",
      TRUE ~ "At"
    )
  )

dist_freq <- dist_data %>%
  group_by(Scorer, Distance_to_Median, Direction) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

p <- ggplot(dist_freq, aes(x = Scorer, y = Distance_to_Median)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = Direction), stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = 4, color = "black", size = 5) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Frequency", range = c(0.012, 25)) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Direction", values = dir_pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = -6:6) +
  labs(x = "Scorer", y = "Distance to Median") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )
p
save_plot(p, "dist_from_median_freq.png", width = 10, height = 14)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows the disagreement patterns between each scorer and the median score.
- For all scorers, the most common outcome was agreement of the median.
- Some scorers (e.g. Scorer 5) tend to score higher than the median. Other scorers (e.g. Scorer 4) tend to score lower than the median.
- Occasionally, some scorers collect scores that are very far from the median - 4, 5, or even 6 scores away.

### 5.2 Signed distance from median by scorer (percentage heatmap)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=13}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 13
# 5.2
dist_pct <- dist_freq %>%
  group_by(Scorer) %>%
  mutate(proportion = Count / sum(Count))

scorer_totals <- dist_freq %>%
  group_by(Scorer) %>%
  summarise(Total = sum(Count), .groups = "drop")

ymin <- min(dist_pct$Distance_to_Median)
ymax <- max(dist_pct$Distance_to_Median)

p <- ggplot(dist_pct, aes(x = Scorer, y = Distance_to_Median, fill = proportion * 100)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", proportion * 100)), color = "black", size = 4, vjust = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    data = scorer_totals, aes(x = Scorer, y = ymax + 0.9, label = paste0("n=", Total)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(name = "Percentage", low = "white", high = "firebrick") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = ymin:ymax, limits = c(ymin - 0.5, ymax + 1.3), expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_equal(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Scorer", y = "Distance to Median") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
p
save_plot(p, "dist_from_median_pct.png", width = 10, height = 13, dir = "thesis_plots")
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot also shows the disagreement patterns between scorers and the median, but as a percentage rather than an absolute count. This makes it clearer to compare distributions between scorers.
- Scorer 5 agrees with the median far less often than any other scorers - only 51.3% of the time. Of the remaining 48.7%, 48.4% of the time they score above the median, and 0.3% below.

### 5.3 Absolute distance from median by median score (bubble)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=10}

#| fig-height: 10

absdist_freq <- absdist_data %>%

  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

p <- ggplot(absdist_freq, aes(x = Median_Score, y = Distance_to_Median)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = factor(Median_Score)), stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = 4, color = "black", size = 5) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Frequency", range = c(3, 25)) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Median\nScore", values = sev_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(x = "Median Score", y = "Absolute Distance from Median") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.25, 6), ylim = c(-0.25, 6))
p
save_plot(p, "abs_dist_by_median.png", width = 10, height = 10)
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows how often disagreeing scores are chosen for each median score.
- Agreement with the median is the most common outcome for every score level.
- 99.8% (3017/3035) of median-0 CDAs were scored within ±1 of the median. Score 3 had the lowest within-±1 rate at 94.4% (1987/2104).
- Score 5 had the largest percentage of disagreeing scores at 35.2%, closely followed by score 2 at 34.8%, compared to only 4.0% for score 0.

### 5.4 Absolute distance from median by median score (percentage heatmap)

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10
# 5.4
absdist_pct <- absdist_freq %>%
  group_by(Median_Score) %>%
  mutate(proportion = Count / sum(Count))

median_totals <- absdist_freq %>%
  group_by(Median_Score) %>%
  summarise(Total = sum(Count), .groups = "drop")

ymax <- max(absdist_pct$Distance_to_Median)

p <- ggplot(absdist_pct, aes(x = factor(Median_Score), y = Distance_to_Median, fill = proportion * 100)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", proportion * 100)), color = "black", size = 4, vjust = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    data = median_totals, aes(x = factor(Median_Score), y = ymax + 0.9, label = paste0("n=", Total)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(name = "Percentage", low = "white", high = "firebrick") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:ymax, limits = c(-0.5, ymax + 1.3), expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_equal(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Median Score", y = "Absolute Distance from Median") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
p
save_plot(p, "abs_dist_by_median_pct.png", width = 10, height = 10, dir = "thesis_plots")
```

**What this shows:**

- This plot shows what proportion of the time disagreeing scores were chosen for each median score.
- The extreme scores 0 and 6 were agreed upon much more often than the intermediate scores.
- The counts represent all the annotations that were involved in cell death areas of each median score (e.g. not all the median-1 cell death area received three 1s, which is why the number differs from the raw count of 1s collected).

---

## 6. Discussion

### 6.1 Score distributions

- The score distributions collected reflect experimental design and biological outcomes. Some experiments have quite binary outcomes (0 or 6) whilst others have more balanced phenotypes, showing a range of intermediate scores.
- A score of 0 is common because of both experimental (intentional negative control included in all experiments) and biological (no expression or no immune response) outcomes.

### 6.2 Differences between scorers

- The differences in the score distributions collected by each scorer could be down to the images they were randomly allocated, but it could also reflect differences in scoring strategy or interpretation of the scoring key.
- The distribution of scores may be due to the random allocation of images during the collection process. The images came from a series of different projects in the Banfield lab, which worked with different biological systems that may show different phenotypic distributions.
- The difference in overall score count are due to three scorers (1, 5, and 7) only scoring one of the two datasets.

### 6.3 Scoring disagreement

- Scoring disagreement may arise due to individual (scoring biases driven by past scoring experiences) or experimental (ambiguous scoring key interpreted differently by different scorers) reasons.
- Score 0 is more unambiguous than intermediate scores. It is a complete lack of cell death area. This may be why cell death areas with a median score of 0 saw fewer disagreeing scores.
- Cell death areas with median 0 scores receive far less scoring variance, and almost nothing beyond the adjacent score. It is an unambiguous task.
- Intermediate scores, which may be more subjective or less clearly align to the scoring key, are scored less consistently.

### 6.4 Missing scores

- Missed scores represent intentional choices, not accidental omissions.
- The annotation tool includes a skip button which the annotators were instructed use for cell death areas that were highly unclear (e.g. leaf folding), damaged, or overlapping with adjacent cell death areas. Different interpretations of these descriptions may account for the variable skip counts.
- Score 0 was the most common score collected, so it being the most commonly missed makes sense. Damaged leaves (often caused by the agroinfiltration syringe puncturing the leaf) also often appeared as score 0.
